title: Unified Inference: Product Overview, PRD, Roadmap, Pricing & Release Notes
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This document consolidates the product-level overview, key PRD items and requirements, high-level design specs, multi-quarter roadmap and themes, pricing & packaging notes, and the most recent release notes for the Unified Inference product family (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). It is intended for product, engineering, sales, and support stakeholders and should be used as the authoritative single-source-of-truth for roadmap planning and customer communications.

Summary / TL;DR
- Goal: Provide a single runtime and developer experience that delivers predictable latency, scalable throughput, and cost-efficient inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.
- Focus areas for next 6-12 months: performance SLOs for 99th p50 latency windows, cost controls (Optimize vX batching + cache), enterprise private deployments (VPC + KMS), and packaging/pricing updates for reserved capacity.
- Release cadence: quarterly feature releases with monthly patch releases for critical fixes.

Audience
- Primary: Product managers, Eng (runtime, infra, platform), Sales, Solutions, Customer Success, Security.

Goals & Success Metrics
- Reliability: Platform-wide 99.95% uptime for hosted inference and Dedicated capacity availability target of 99.9%.
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 generation latency targets by traffic class (see SLOs below).
- Cost Efficiency: Reduce per-token serving cost by 18% YoY via batching, KV caching, and quantization recommendations.
- Adoption: Increase Dedicated pipeline contracts by 30% and Private deployments by 25% across regulated accounts year-over-year.

1) Product Requirements (PRD)
---------------------------
Purpose: Define customer-facing capabilities and non-functional requirements required for the next major release (v4.0).

Key user stories (prioritized)
- As an ML engineer I want a single REST SDK call to switch routing policies (latency vs cost) so my service can trade off price and latency dynamically.
- As a platform engineer I need predictable throughput guarantees for Reserved Dedicated pools to plan downstream services.
- As a compliance lead I need audit logs and KMS integration for Private deployments.
- As an SRE I need improved observability (token-level cost attribution) and tracing hooks to reduce MTTR.

Non-functional requirements
- SLOs: see metrics table.
- Security: Private deployments must support customer-managed KMS and TLS 1.3 only by default.
- Scalability: Must support autoregression workloads up to 10k concurrent requests per cluster with <3% tail increase.
- Backwards compatibility: API v1 endpoints remain supported; deprecation timeline for v1.1 features must be 6 months.

Requirements table (key acceptance criteria)
| ID | Requirement | Owner | Acceptance Criteria |
| R-001 | Routing policy switch (latency/cost) | product/eng-runtime | API documented, end-to-end tests, <10ms additional overhead to routing decision |
| R-002 | Dedicated capacity SLAs | eng-sre/product | SLA in billing UI, config for reserved GPU pool sizes, test harness for load |
| R-003 | Private KMS + audit logs | eng-private-deployments/security | KMS integration documented, logs exported to customer SIEM, E2E runbook |
| R-004 | Token-level cost attribution | eng-platform | Console shows token cost by route/model, daily export to billing pipeline |
| R-005 | Quantization recommendation engine | applied-ml | Recommendation UI and CLI, validated on representative workloads with regression tolerance <= 1% |

Prioritization & Scope
- Must-have (MVP for v4.0): R-001, R-002, R-003, R-004
- Should-have (v4.x): R-005, advanced batching policies, canary rollout tooling for model variants
- Nice-to-have (future): per-customer prefix cache profiles, automatic mixed-precision conversion for customer models

2) High-level Design Specs
--------------------------
Design principles: safety-first (regression guardrails), developer ergonomics, and measurable economics.

Architecture components (high-level)
- API Gateway: rate limiting, auth, routing policy decisions.
- Router/Policy Engine: evaluates latency vs cost preferences, selects model variant and region.
- Serving Runtime: continuous batching, KV cache, optimized kernels.
- Dedicated Scheduler: manages reserved GPU pools with autoscale headroom.
- Private Control Plane: customer-specific config, KMS connectors, audit log exporter.

API & Contract changes
- New field on POST /v1/generate: "routing_priority" with values ["latency", "cost", "balanced"]. Default "balanced" for backward compatibility.
- Response now includes: "model_variant_id", "routing_decision_reason", and optional "cache_hit": true|false.
- SDK changes: add client.reroutePolicy = client.setRoutingPriority(...) with examples in Python/Node.

Design considerations & tradeoffs
- Preference evaluation must be sub-10ms; use cached decision trees and async policy refresh.
- Adding routing metadata increases response size ~120 bytes on average; acceptable for our use cases but logged sizes must be monitored.

Security & Compliance
- Private deployments: require FIPS2 KMS adapters and customer-provided certs.
- Audit log schema versioned; default retention 365 days for enterprise customers (configurable).

3) Roadmap & Themes (next 4 quarters)
-------------------------------------
Q3 2028 (current): Launch v4.0 (Routing policies, Dedicated SLA, KMS + audit) — GA June 30 2028
Q4 2028: Redwood Optimize v3 integration (automated batching configs + quantization suggestions), improved cost analytics
Q1 2029: Private on-prem appliance beta (air-gapped), tenant-level prefix caching pilot
Q2 2029: Model variant marketplace + A/B rollout improvements, longer-term compression profiles

Roadmap themes by target outcome
- Performance & Reliability: reduce p99 latency by 20% on high-throughput workloads
- Cost Optimization: automated recommendations to cut serving cost per 1M tokens by 15%
- Enterprise Readiness: expanded compliance and VPC/hybrid deployment tooling

Release cadence & gates
- Feature freeze 4 weeks before GA.
- Required gates: perf bench (no >5% regression vs baseline), security review completed, customer pilot signoff for enterprise features.

4) Pricing & Packaging Notes
---------------------------
Summary of proposed changes for v4.0:
- Hosted API: keep per-token pricing but add "Routing Premium" optional toggle for lowest-latency routing at +20% cost on affected tokens.
- Dedicated: introduce 3 commitment tiers (Standard, Business, Enterprise) with sliding discounts for reserved GPU-months and included burst credits.
- Private: license + support model; base platform fee + per-node compute warranty + optional compliance bundle.

Pricing table (illustrative)
| Tier | Billing Model | Commit Term | Notes |
| Hosted (base) | per-token | n/a | default curated models |
| Hosted (latency premium) | per-token + premium | monthly opt-in | routes to lower latency variants or priority capacity |
| Dedicated - Standard | reserved GPU-month | 1/12 months | minimal SLA, standard support |
| Dedicated - Business | reserved GPU-month | 12/24 months | 99.9% availability, priority onboarding |
| Private | license + node | annual | includes private control plane and basic support |

Discounting & packaging rules
- 12-month commitments get 18% discount; 24-month commit 30%.
- Bundled Optimize credit tiers available for Dedicated Business & Enterprise customers.

Billing & metering changes
- New meter: "routing_priority_premium_tokens" to track premium-latency token usage.
- Export daily usage lines to billing pipeline; include token-level breakdown by model_variant_id.

5) Release notes (v4.0 — GA 2028-06-30)
------------------------------------
Highlights
- Added routing_priority API field (latency/cost/balanced) and console controls.
- Dedicated capacity SLA and dedicated pool autoscale improvements.
- Private deployment: KMS integration, audit log export, and new on-prem packaging guide.
- Console: token-level cost attribution and per-route dashboards.

Notable bug fixes
- Fixed race condition in KV cache invalidation impacting warm-start latency.
- Resolved rare OOM when serving very long-context (>=32k) requests in mixed-precision paths.

Migration notes for customers
1. API: routing_priority defaults to "balanced". No action required for existing integrations unless you want to opt into latency premium.
2. Dedicated customers: review SLA and update billing commitments in the console.
3. Private: new KMS connectors require configuration prior to upgrade; see "onprem-packaging/kms-integration" runbook.

6) Rollout Plan & Post-release Operations
----------------------------------------
Canary rollout steps (2-phase)
1. Internal canary: 5% of internal traffic routed to v4.0 for 72 hours. Monitor perf and error budgets.
2. External canary: 10% of customer traffic (pilot customers) for 7 days.
3. Progressive ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 weeks if no regressions.

Gating metrics (sample)
- p50/p95/p99 latency by model_class (baseline +5% allowed for p99 during canary).
- Error rate increase <= 0.1% absolute.
- Token cost change monitored; recommend stop-if >10% unexpected increase per route.

Rollback plan
1. Emergency rollback: revert router policy to previous stable build and route traffic to prior model variants.
2. If rollback fails, drain new nodes and re-attach old replicas.

Post-release: 30/60 day check-ins with pilot customers, collect regressions via evals harness, and ship hotfixes monthly as required.

8) Metrics & Dashboards to Monitor
----------------------------------
- Per-route token throughput and latency (p50/p95/p99) rendered in Console.
- Token-level cost by model_variant_id (daily export).
- Dedicated pool utilization and reserved capacity headroom.
- Audit log export success rate for Private customers.

9) Risks & Mitigations
----------------------
- Risk: Routing decisions add latency and complexity. Mitigation: cache policy decisions, keep decision path lightweight, and include fallback to "balanced" if policy engine times out.
- Risk: Customers see higher token cost after default suggestions. Mitigation: provide simulation tool in Console to preview cost changes and opt-in prompts.
